title: Image availability is not visual proof; inspect the current artifact before acting
inherited_objective: Determine what the current image or contact sheet visibly proves, then choose the next task action from that observation.
live_state: A tool result or internal record can say that an image exists without exposing its pixels to the reviewer.
A latest/index lookup and a direct image or contact-sheet open are available as the shortest evidence path.
No transport outage has been established; base64, MCP, and downloader work would be an unrequested expansion.
The screenshot's semantics may contradict the prior narrative, so the pixels outrank the narrative.
user_correction: Inspect the actual current image through the shortest direct evidence path, state what is visibly shown, and use that observation for the next action.
protected_state: Existing preserved evidence and artifact identity
The distinction between internal availability and user-visible proof
hard_exclusions: Do not promote tool metadata, file existence, or an HTTP/MCP success into visual proof.
Do not add base64 encoding, MCP transport, downloaders, or infrastructure when a current image is already available.
Do not fit screenshot semantics to a prior narrative or omit contradictory visible details.
Do not name a human-facing reviewed artifact with only an opaque hash.

failure_candidate.action: Treat internal image availability as user-visible success, expand into base64/MCP transport work, and describe the screenshot according to the prior narrative without opening it.
failure_candidate.why_wrong: The candidate never establishes what the current pixels show, changes the task into transport engineering, and makes an unsupported visual claim.

trace.details: The image proof passes because the tool reported it available.
Invent base64/MCP/download transport to obtain an image that was already available.
Repeat the expected screenshot story without inspecting screenshot semantics.

success_candidate.action: Read the latest/index record, open the current image or contact sheet directly, record the visible screenshot semantics, name the reviewed artifact descriptively with its date, and choose the next action from those observations.
success_candidate.why_correct: The sequence proves the user-visible evidence at the correct layer, preserves the existing objective, avoids transport scope expansion, and lets current pixels falsify stale narrative.

trace.details: Resolve the newest preserved artifact from the current index before opening it.
Open the resolved current image/contact sheet through the shortest available direct evidence path.
State visible composition, UI/screenshot semantics, contradictions, and any unreadable or missing regions.
Derive a human-facing descriptive name only after inspection; retain hash/provenance separately.
Use the recorded visible result to decide the next task action and keep unproven claims explicit.

discriminating_evidence: Whether a latest/index record was read before choosing the artifact
Whether the current image/contact sheet was opened directly and its pixels inspected
The written visible observations, including screenshot semantics that contradict the prior narrative
Whether any base64/MCP/download transport was invented despite direct availability
The reviewed artifact name and its separate hash/provenance record
completion_condition: A current reviewed artifact has a dated descriptive name, its visible semantics are recorded, and the next action is explicitly based on those observations rather than metadata or narrative.
